title: Jain Realties
description: Jain Realties is a Nagpur-based real estate brand focused on premium residential projects. My role was to create a strong and consistent visual identity across their digital and outdoor marketing, with a design direction focused on premium, classy and aspirational communication.
challenge: The brand needed social media creatives that could communicate the premium lifestyle and value of its real estate projects while standing out in a highly competitive real estate market. The key challenge was to move beyond generic property advertisements and create visuals that felt premium, sophisticated and brand-led.
approach: I developed a visual direction centered around premium & classy aesthetics, strong typography, high-quality property visuals, sophisticated colour combinations, clean visual hierarchy, aspirational lifestyle communication and consistent brand presentation. Every creative was designed to make the property feel more than just a building — a premium lifestyle investment.

What I designed spans social media posts (campaign creatives, promotional posts, property highlights and engagement-focused content), Instagram stories (interactive and visually engaging stories for property promotion, campaigns and brand communication) and billboards & outdoor creatives (large-format advertising with strong visual impact and quick readability).

Premium doesn't mean complicated — it means every visual element feels intentional. I focused on creating designs with enough visual breathing room while using typography, imagery and composition to communicate luxury and trust.
outcome: Social media posts, Instagram stories and outdoor creatives designed with a consistent, premium visual direction for a real estate brand.

title: The Wild Cafe
description: The Wild Cafe is a cafe brand focused on creating a memorable and inviting experience for its customers. I worked on developing engaging visual creatives that helped the brand communicate its offers, ambience and overall personality across both digital and offline touchpoints.
challenge: The brand needed visually appealing marketing creatives that could grab attention, communicate offers quickly and encourage customers to visit and engage with the cafe. The challenge was to create designs that felt fresh, attractive and consistent while working across different formats.
approach: I created a visual direction that focused on eye-catching compositions, appetizing food & beverage presentation, strong typography, clear promotional messaging, consistent brand styling, social-media-friendly layouts and high-impact offline advertising.

What I designed spans social media stories (promotional and engagement-focused stories built to capture attention and drive visits), posters (campaign and promotional posters designed for high visual impact), banners (digital and promotional banners communicating offers and campaigns) and standee designs (offline promotional creatives to attract attention inside and around the cafe).
outcome: Social media stories, posters, banners and standees designed for a cafe brand, covering both digital and in-store formats.

title: Atulya Jewellers
description: Atulya Jewellers is a jewellery brand where the visual presentation plays an important role in communicating luxury, elegance and trust. I worked on the brand's social media design, creating premium and visually consistent content to strengthen its digital presence.
challenge: Jewellery is a highly visual category, so the social media presence needed to feel premium, sophisticated and aspirational while keeping the jewellery itself at the center of attention. The goal was to create content that looked polished and consistent across the brand's social platforms.
approach: I developed creatives around luxury-focused visual compositions, elegant typography, premium colour combinations, high-quality jewellery presentation, clean layouts and visual hierarchy, festive & occasion-based creatives and consistent social media aesthetics.

What I designed spans social media posts (premium product showcases, promotional creatives and brand communication), social media stories (engaging story designs for products, occasions, campaigns and festive communication) and campaign creatives (visually strong creatives built around important jewellery campaigns and occasions).
outcome: Social media posts, stories and campaign creatives designed with a consistent, premium look for a jewellery brand.

title: SDPL
description: SDPL is a real estate brand for which I worked across multiple marketing touchpoints, creating a consistent and premium visual presence across digital, social media and outdoor advertising. The objective was to present the brand and its properties in a visually engaging way while maintaining consistency across different formats.
challenge: Real estate marketing requires creatives that can communicate property value, lifestyle and key information quickly while still looking premium and attention-grabbing. The challenge was to adapt the brand communication across multiple platforms and formats without losing visual consistency.
approach: I developed a visual communication system focused on premium property presentation, strong typography & hierarchy, high-impact compositions, consistent brand styling, lifestyle-focused visuals, promotional storytelling and AI-assisted visual content.

What I designed spans social media designs (property promotions, campaigns, informative posts and engagement-focused creatives), AI videos (AI-assisted promotional videos and visual storytelling showcasing properties in a more engaging format), banners & posters (high-impact promotional creatives for campaigns and property communication), standee designs (print-ready promotional designs for on-ground marketing and property events) and hoarding designs (large-format outdoor creatives for maximum visibility and quick communication).
outcome: A consistent visual language applied across social media, AI video, print and outdoor advertising for a real estate brand.

title: Bon Patisserie
description: Bon Patisserie is a cafe brand that wanted its digital presence to feel funky, playful and creative rather than following a conventional cafe design style. I worked on creating visually expressive social media content that captured the brand's personality and made each creative instantly eye-catching.
challenge: The key challenge was to make the brand stand out in a crowded food & cafe space while keeping the communication fun, energetic and visually memorable.
approach: I explored a bold visual direction using funky compositions, playful typography, vibrant visual elements, creative food presentation, unexpected layouts, strong colour combinations and social-first compositions. The goal was to make every post feel like a piece of creative content, not just a promotional advertisement.

What I designed spans social media graphics (creative posts built around products, promotions and brand communication) and posters (bold promotional posters with expressive layouts and strong visual hierarchy). Design objective: make the brand feel as exciting visually as the experience it offers.
outcome: Bringing a funky, playful visual personality to Bon Patisserie through bold social media and campaign design — helping the brand feel as exciting visually as the experience it offers.

title: Airtel — App Download Post
altText: Airtel — App Download Post — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post promoting the Airtel app for mobile recharge, bill payments, broadband and digital services.
challenge: Say what the app does and get people to download it, in one glance.
approach: I put the phone and the Airtel logo large on a bold red background, with a three-line headline and a clear download button, plus a service strip at the bottom.
outcome: A clean, high-contrast app promotion post in the brand's red and white.

title: Premium Row Houses
altText: Premium Row Houses — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for premium row houses, with the home shown as the main visual and the key details kept short.
challenge: Make a real estate post feel premium and easy to read, with the property doing most of the talking.
approach: I used a full-bleed photo of the house with a blue sky, kept the headline at the top left, and listed the home types and features in small highlighted chips, with contact details at the bottom.
outcome: A premium-looking property post where the home is clear and the contact details are easy to find.

title: French Essence — Oud Rush
altText: French Essence — Oud Rush — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for a luxury fragrance, Oud Rush by French Essence, built around the bottle.
challenge: Show a perfume in a way that feels rich and desirable, using only an image and a few words.
approach: I placed the bottle at the centre on a warm gold-and-black background with a golden drip of oil, and kept the text to a headline and one short line.
outcome: A dark, premium fragrance post with the product as the one clear focus.

title: Dedicated PRO — Simplify Your Business
altText: Dedicated PRO — Simplify Your Business — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for a dedicated PRO service, with the message “Get a Dedicated PRO — Simplify Your Business”.
challenge: Explain a business service visually and keep the message simple.
approach: I showed a relaxed professional with a laptop on a cloud above a city skyline, with a bold headline and the key phrase highlighted in a red box.
outcome: A light, friendly post that makes a business service feel easy.

title: Property AI
altText: Property AI — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for Property AI, an AI-powered platform for discovering, evaluating and growing real estate opportunities.
challenge: Present an AI product for real estate in a way that feels modern but still trustworthy.
approach: I used a glass-fronted building at dusk with an orange glow on a dark background, and three short benefit tiles under the headline.
outcome: A modern tech-meets-property post with a clear headline and three easy-to-scan benefits.

title: Airtel — Data Plans
altText: Airtel — Data Plans — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post about Airtel data plans, with quick actions for buying data, buying airtime, checking balance and contacting support.
challenge: Show several actions in one post without it looking crowded.
approach: I placed a person on a red chair at the centre and arranged four rounded action buttons around her, with the headline in a red bubble above.
outcome: A playful, organised post that shows what the app can do at a glance.

title: Agentic AI for Enterprises
altText: Agentic AI for Enterprises — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post about agentic AI for enterprises, listing five benefits for modern businesses.
challenge: Make a technical AI topic look clear and strong, not complicated.
approach: I used a glowing AI figure on a dark background with orange light, a large headline, and five short points with simple icons.
outcome: A bold, dark tech post that keeps a complex topic easy to scan.

title: Hire Faster. Manage Smarter.
altText: Hire Faster. Manage Smarter. — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for end-to-end HR solutions for growing businesses, under the headline “Hire Faster. Manage Smarter.”
challenge: Make an HR service feel modern and approachable.
approach: I used a purple gradient with a relaxed professional at a desk, and a two-line headline with the second line in a lighter colour.
outcome: A clean, colourful HR service post with a headline that is easy to remember.

title: Blinkit — Delivered in 10 Minutes
altText: Blinkit — Delivered in 10 Minutes — social media post design by Bittu Rai
description: A social media post for Blinkit, built around the message “Everything You Need Delivered in 10 Minutes”.
challenge: Communicate speed and variety for a quick-delivery app in one post.
approach: I used a bright yellow background with two app screens in front and a person sitting on a sofa, with the “10 Minutes” part highlighted in green.
outcome: A bright, energetic quick-commerce post that puts the delivery promise first.

title: Zest
description: A social media post for Zest, my college fest, designed to stand out in students' crowded feeds.
challenge: The post had to grab attention among hundreds of other event posts on students' feeds, and the key details still had to be readable at thumbnail size.
approach: I kept the design bold and energetic, using bright colours and strong typography to match the excitement of the fest. Key event details were placed in a clear hierarchy so they stay readable even as a small thumbnail.
outcome: A bold, easy-to-scan fest post, and one of my early lessons in designing for a crowded, fast-scrolling feed.

title: Sponsorship Invitation — Nakash Aziz Live
description: A sponsorship invitation for a live concert at my college fest, Zest, made to be sent to potential sponsors and brands.
challenge: It had to look credible to a business audience while still carrying the fest's energetic branding.
approach: I kept the layout structured and professional, and arranged the essentials — artist, date, venue and contact — so they can be scanned in seconds.
outcome: An invitation designed to make sponsors take the opportunity seriously at first glance.

title: FlashAid Ads
description: An ad creative for a client whose main requirement was performance — the design needed to convert, not just look good.
challenge: The creative had to communicate its offer almost instantly and push people to act, rather than just look attractive.
approach: I focused on a clear value proposition up top, a strong-contrast call-to-action and minimal distractions around it, based on what typically performs well in paid social. Colour and copy hierarchy were arranged so the offer is understood in under two seconds.
outcome: A clean, conversion-focused ad that puts clarity ahead of pure aesthetics.

title: Jewellery
description: A social media post for a jewellery client who wanted a classy, premium look.
challenge: The post had to feel premium, never cheap or cluttered, with the product as the clear focus.
approach: I leaned into darker tones, subtle metallic accents and generous spacing — the visual language I use across most of my jewellery and luxury work. The product stays the visual focus, with type and graphics in a supporting role, and every choice from font weight to spacing was made with restraint.
outcome: A premium-feeling post that shows how tone and restraint can make a design feel luxurious.

title: Selected Demo Post
description: A self-initiated demo post, created without a live client brief to show my design range.
challenge: With no client brief, the goal was to show range and get selected for design opportunities by treating the post like a real project.
approach: I picked a concept, researched references and refined the layout through multiple iterations before finalising it.
outcome: A self-initiated demo post, created to practise and demonstrate a design process.

title: Natural Product
description: A post for a natural product brand that wanted a unique ad showing the product in enough detail to explain what it does.
challenge: Show the product clearly enough that people understand what it does and why it's different, instead of just decorating it.
approach: I researched how similar natural and organic product brands present ingredients and benefits visually, then built a layout that balances product photography with clear, scannable text.
outcome: A post that informs as much as it attracts, with the product's story clear at a glance.

title: Stories Shaping Tomorrow
description: A TEDx post made for a founder speaker, with one instruction: keep it simple, with her face as the main focus.
challenge: Keep the design simple and make the speaker, not the graphics, the focal point.
approach: I designed the layout around her portrait first, then added minimal supporting text and the TEDx branding without letting it compete with her. Typography stays understated so the focus never shifts away from the speaker.
outcome: A clean speaker post designed around a person's presence rather than around graphics.

title: Design Post
description: A post for a jewellery brand that wanted its pieces shown in a premium, classy design.
challenge: Reflect the craftsmanship of the product and give the jewellery centre stage.
approach: I built the layout around close, detailed product shots on a dark, neutral background so the jewellery pops without extra noise. Typography and spacing were kept minimal and elegant, in line with the premium tone the client asked for.
outcome: A post that positions the jewellery as the centrepiece, exactly as the brief required.

title: Real Estate
description: A post for a real estate brand that wanted a premium, unique design with a sense of nature.
challenge: Move away from the usual plain floor-plan style post while keeping a premium tone.
approach: I researched how upscale real estate brands blend architecture with natural elements like greenery, sky and light, then built a layout combining property visuals with organic textures. The typography stays clean and confident to match the premium tone.
outcome: A real estate post that pushes beyond the category's usual visual clichés.

title: Aditya Ortho — Storefront Signage & Print Set
altText: Aditya Ortho storefront mockup with red and yellow signage, window graphics and standees, designed by Bittu Rai
description: Aditya Ortho is a multi-service centre in Bokaro offering insurance services, orthopedic products, and print, xerox and lamination. This is the full signage and print set designed for its shop: main signboard, window graphic, vertical standees, strip signs and service cards. The first image is a storefront mockup showing how it comes together.
challenge: One small shop had to explain three different things at a glance: insurance services, orthopedic products and print services, on signs of very different sizes and shapes.
approach: I built one red and yellow visual system and reused it on every piece: the shop name in bold white and yellow, services in clear icon rows, and the 20% offer as a bright yellow highlight. Each file was laid out at its own print size, from a 12 × 1 ft strip to an 8 × 7 ft banner, so the hierarchy stays readable from the street.
outcome: A print-ready set in nine sizes: an 11 × 3 ft main signboard, an 8 × 7 ft banner, a 12 × 1 ft strip, two 2 × 7 ft standees, two 11.8 inch × 12 ft vertical signs and two 3.75 × 2.3 inch cards (services and contact).

title: Zest Fest Invitation
description: My college fest invite, designed as a single collage banner that brings every Zest event into one shareable visual.
challenge: It needed to work both as a print banner and as a shareable social invite.
approach: I approached it the same way as my Zest poster, gathering visuals from each event and arranging them with clear hierarchy so the fest name stands out first, and kept text legible at multiple sizes.
outcome: One asset that works across two different formats.

title: INDUS AVIVA
description: Indus Aviva is an Indian water storage tank manufacturer that wanted a minimal, premium look for its company profile.
challenge: Present an affordable but quality-focused manufacturer in a minimal, premium and professional way.
approach: I started by understanding their positioning, then researched how similar B2B manufacturing brands present themselves professionally. I kept the layout clean and spacious, using generous white space and a simple grid so the document feels premium and easy to navigate. The final profile reflects the brand's mission of accessibility and quality without feeling cluttered.
outcome: Welcome to Indus Aviva, where kindness and a desire to make a difference drive our mission. Our name reflects our Indian heritage and our commitment to ushering in a new era of hope and renewal for the common man. The name Aviva, meaning "a new springtime," symbolizes our desire to bring about positive change in the lives of those we serve. The COVID-19 pandemic inspired us to contribute to our society, realizing that earning from business enables us to provide meaningful support. We established Indus Aviva in 2021, focusing on manufacturing superior, affordable, and accessible water storage tanks for all.

title: Abgelica Enterprises
description: Abgelica Enterprises is a Delhi-headquartered manpower supply company serving clients across India.
challenge: The brief was for a very classy, simple design that's easy to understand at a glance.
approach: I researched how established B2B service companies structure their profiles — services, experience and sectors served — and organised the content in that same logical, scannable order. Typography and colour were kept restrained so the document reads as professional and trustworthy rather than flashy. The result is a company profile a decision-maker can skim in minutes and still walk away with a clear picture of the business.
outcome: We are one of the reputed manpower supply companies in India, headquartered in Delhi, focused on providing manpower supply services throughout India for the past 12 years. We are the one-stop solution for manpower supply in India, meeting the requirement of general and technical services for all major industrial sectors such as Facilities Management, Manpower & Security Service, and Horticulture & Exhibition Services. With over 12 years of service, we provide skilled and unskilled labour across different industrial sectors. Our goal is to provide quality manpower supply services to all our clients in India.

title: LOOP — Urban Cycling Club
description: LOOP is an urban cycling club built around community, movement and the love of riding in the city. I designed its complete brand identity — logo, colour palette, graphic patterns, social media look and brand applications — to feel energetic, modern and confident.
challenge: The club needed a recognisable identity that could work everywhere a cycling community shows up: on jerseys and bikes, at events, on social media and inside an app, while expressing movement, freedom and togetherness.
approach: The logo combines a continuous, infinity-inspired symbol with the idea of cycling. The symbol sits inside the wordmark and works on its own as an icon, representing endless movement, balance and the connection between riders and the city.

A vibrant orange stands for energy, enthusiasm and adventure, supported by black, light grey and white. Bold, modern typography keeps the brand confident, and a flowing wave shape, geometric forms and a repeating loop pattern give the identity a consistent visual language.

I then applied the system across touchpoints: an Instagram profile with highlight icons and a post grid, posters and campaign creatives ("Keep The City Moving", "A Community for Urban Cyclists"), event branding with a stage backdrop, bike, water bottle and feather flag, rider jerseys, and an app icon.
outcome: A complete brand identity for LOOP Urban Cycling Club, including logo and icon, colour palette, patterns, social media design and event, apparel and app applications, presented as a brand identity case study.

title: Pebble — by roshni studio
description: Pebble by roshni studio is a kids' interior brand that creates thoughtful, playful and functional spaces for children. I designed its complete brand identity — logo, colour palette, typography and supporting visual assets — to feel warm, creative and child-friendly.
challenge: The brand needed to feel playful enough for children while still looking calm, trustworthy and well-designed for the parents who choose the interiors.
approach: I built the logo around a simple story: stacked pebbles, a little house, a sun and a growing plant, all drawn with soft, hand-made lines. The wordmark uses rounded, multi-coloured letters that echo the pebbles and keep the brand friendly.

The colour palette (coral #FF6B61, yellow #FFC34D, blue #6EC1E4 and green #97B487) is inspired by childhood, nature and creativity. Nunito (ExtraBold / Bold) and Poppins (Regular / Medium) pair soft, rounded headings with clean, readable body text.

To make the brand flexible, I added logo variations (icon only, black & white and a reversed version on coral) and a set of supporting visual assets — a pebble shape, sun, leaf, stacked pebbles and waves — for use across digital and physical touchpoints.
outcome: A complete brand identity for Pebble, including logo and logo variations, colour palette, typography and supporting visual assets, presented as a brand guidelines deck.

title: Artham Infrastructure
description: Artham Infrastructure needed a complete brand identity — logo, colours and visual system — to represent a growing infrastructure company.
challenge: Stand out in a competitive, mostly unbranded industry where trust is everything.
approach: I started by understanding their positioning, then researched how larger infrastructure and construction brands build trust visually through strong, geometric marks and confident colour palettes. The logo and system were designed to feel stable and credible.
outcome: Designed a complete brand identity for Artham Infrastructure, including logo mark, colour palette and visual system built to feel solid, trustworthy and consistent across every touchpoint, from stationery to site signage.

title: Shri Amar Sai Resort
description: Shri Amar Sai Resort needed a brand identity that reflects hospitality and comfort rather than a corporate feel.
challenge: Build an emotional connection with guests before they even arrive, without a corporate look.
approach: I researched how resort and hospitality brands use warmer colours, softer typography and welcoming visual cues. The logo and colour system were designed to feel inviting and premium at the same time, matching the resort's positioning.
outcome: Designed a complete brand identity for Shri Amar Sai Resort, including logo mark, colour palette and visual system built to feel warm and inviting, carrying the resort's identity consistently across signage, print and digital touchpoints.

title: Bhavya Construction Management
description: Bhavya Construction Management needed a brand identity that communicates reliability and scale in the project management niche.
challenge: Most competitors in construction management looked either too corporate or too generic.
approach: I researched competitor branding in the construction management space to find a visual gap, then designed a logo and colour system that feels modern without losing the industry's sense of seriousness. Every element was built to work at both large (signage) and small (business card) scale.
outcome: Designed a complete brand identity for Bhavya Construction Management, including logo mark, colour palette and visual system built to feel professional and dependable across print, digital and site branding.

title: Fitness Tracker App UI/UX Design | Mobile Fitness Experience
altText: Fitness Tracker mobile app UI/UX design by Bittu Rai, with onboarding, workouts and activity dashboard screens
description: A modern Fitness Tracker App designed to make everyday fitness tracking simple, engaging, and motivating. The app features a clean interface with a bold orange and black visual identity, helping users track their daily activity, explore workouts, monitor fitness progress, and stay consistent with their health goals.

Key features: personalized onboarding experience, daily fitness activity dashboard, workout discovery and exercise library, fitness goal tracking, progress monitoring and statistics, and clean, intuitive mobile navigation.
challenge: Fitness apps often feel crowded, with workouts, stats and goals all competing for attention. I wanted a mobile app where a user sees today's progress and the next workout at a glance.
approach: I designed three connected screens in Figma: a bold onboarding screen, a workouts screen with search, category filters and a resume-last-workout card, and a daily dashboard with calories burned, a streak tracker and activity tiles for steps, active minutes and intake. An orange and black palette keeps the key numbers large and easy to read.
outcome: A clean mobile UI where a user can check progress, pick a workout and keep a streak without digging through menus. As a personal concept, it has not been tested with users and has no usage numbers to share.

title: School Management Dashboard UI/UX Design | Admin Panel
altText: School Management admin dashboard UI/UX design by Bittu Rai, with student, finance, fee and calendar screens
description: A modern School Management Admin Dashboard designed to simplify daily school operations and give administrators a centralized platform to manage students, teachers, finances, attendance, and academic activities. The dashboard focuses on a clean layout, intuitive navigation, and data visualization to make school management more organized and efficient.

Key features: overview dashboard with student, teacher and employee statistics, student management and registration, finance and fee management, earnings and expense analytics, notice board and announcements, calendar and timetable management, fee status tracking, and a messages and communication panel.
challenge: School admins handle students, teachers, fees, notices and timetables, often in separate places. The dashboard had to hold a lot of data without feeling heavy or confusing.
approach: I designed the admin panel in Figma around one sidebar (Dashboard, Teachers, Students, Finance, Calendar, Time Table, Message). The home screen shows student, teacher and employee counts, a notice board, income and expenses, and fee status. I then designed the students list, an add-student form split into clear sections, and a fees management screen with a collection chart and status table. A deep red sidebar and coloured stat cards keep each type of information easy to find.
outcome: A consistent admin panel where the dashboard, student records and fee tracking all follow one system. As a personal concept, it uses sample data and has not been tested with a real school.

title: Netflix UI/UX Redesign Concept
altText: Netflix home page UI/UX redesign concept by Bittu Rai
description: A personal concept in which I redesigned the Netflix home page in Figma, with one goal: help viewers see what is new and trending at a glance.
challenge: The original home page was dense, which made it hard to tell what was new or trending, and it offered no filters to narrow things down.
approach: I restructured the layout so new and trending content stands out, and added filters so viewers can narrow what they see. It is a single-page concept designed in Figma.
outcome: A home page that is easier to scan and more user-friendly. As a personal concept, it has no usage numbers to share.

title: SaaS Company Website UI/UX Design
altText: SaaS company website UI/UX design by Bittu Rai
description: A client project: a website for a SaaS company, designed from scratch in Figma. The client wanted a clear, premium and user-friendly site.
challenge: The client needed a professional website that presents the business well, feels premium and is easy to use.
approach: I designed the whole website from scratch, planning the layout, colours, typography and page flow across 8 pages.
outcome: The client was very happy with the final design and with the response it received.

title: E-Commerce Sign-Up UI/UX Design
altText: Responsive sign-up form UI redesign by Bittu Rai
description: A demo project: I redesigned an old sign-up form into a cleaner, more modern and responsive experience.
challenge: The old sign-up form looked inconsistent and complex, which made it hard to understand.
approach: I redesigned the layout, typography and flow to make the form clear, professional and easy to follow, and made it responsive.
outcome: A simpler, easier-to-understand sign-up form. As a demo project, it has no conversion or sales numbers to share.

title: E-commerce Website UI/UX Design
altText: Plant store e-commerce website UI/UX design by Bittu Rai
description: A demo project: a website UI/UX design for a plant-based company, made in Figma.
challenge: The company wanted to show its plants online. Visitors needed to see categories, plant types and client feedback, and be able to book a plant easily.
approach: I designed the full website, from layout and colours to typography and page flow, across 10 pages.
outcome: A complete 10-page website design that makes browsing and booking simple. As a demo project, it has no live results to report.

title: Fashion Shopping App — Mobile UI/UX Design
altText: Fashion shopping mobile app home screen UI design by Bittu Rai
description: A concept project: the home page of a fashion shopping app, designed in Figma.
challenge: The existing experience had no clear categories or brands, and no defined brand colours or fonts. The goal was a clear, professional and user-friendly design.
approach: I designed the home page layout, set up the brand colours, fonts and visual identity, and made categories and brands clear on the page.
outcome: A clear, consistent home page design for the app. As a concept project, it has no sales or user numbers to share.

title: Dating App — Mobile UI/UX Design
altText: Mobile dating app UI/UX design by Bittu Rai
description: A client project: the full UI/UX design for a dating app built on a different vision from regular dating apps.
challenge: The app needed to stop fake and duplicate profiles, so I had to design a flow where people verify their identity before they can use the app.
approach: I designed the login flow so users verify their Aadhaar card with their photo and only verified users get in. I designed the complete app UI/UX in Figma.
outcome: The full UI/UX design is complete. The app is not live yet, because the client's development team is still building it.

title: WhatsApp Desktop — UI Redesign Concept By Bittu Rai
altText: WhatsApp desktop app UI redesign concept by Bittu Rai
description: A personal concept project: a redesign of WhatsApp Desktop in Figma.
challenge: In the current app, people can confuse Status and chats. I wanted to make each area clearer.
approach: I added separate buttons for Story, Chat and Group, plus a filter. It is a single-screen redesign.
outcome: A concept with clearer navigation between the different areas, made for practice.

title: Shopping App — E-commerce Mobile UI/UX Design
altText: E-commerce shopping mobile app UI design by Bittu Rai
description: A personal concept project: a shopping app UI designed in Figma, exploring a new style and concept.
challenge: The goal was to try a fresh style and a new concept for an e-commerce shopping app.
approach: I designed the app screen in Figma, working on the layout, colours and typography.
outcome: A single-screen concept for a shopping app. It is a demo, so there are no results to report.

title: Consulting Firm Website — Modern UI/UX Design
altText: Consulting firm website redesign UI by Bittu Rai
description: A pitch concept: I redesigned a consulting firm's old website to show them how it could be modernised.
challenge: The firm's old website needed to feel more modern and be more user-friendly.
approach: I redesigned the website with a new style and new animation ideas to make it clearer and easier to use.
outcome: Made only as a pitch, so there are no results to report. It shows how I would modernise an existing website.

title: Buildexa — Construction Company Website UI/UX Design
altText: Buildexa construction company website UI/UX design by Bittu Rai
description: A personal practice project: a website UI/UX design for a construction company, made in Figma.
challenge: I wanted a visitor to understand what the company does within 5 seconds of landing on the site.
approach: I designed the full website, 5 pages in total, with a clear first screen and a simple structure.
outcome: A 5-page website design made for demo and practice. There are no client results to report.

title: Wedding Invitation Website
altText: Wedding invitation website with an opening book animation, invitation and wedding functions screens
description: An interactive digital wedding invitation website. Guests tap a book to open it, then see the invitation, a save-the-date countdown, a swipeable carousel of wedding functions, the schedule, and the venue with directions.
challenge: A paper wedding card is static, and guests then have to ask someone for the dates, functions and venue. I wanted one link that gives guests everything on their phone, with the feel of a traditional invitation.
approach: I designed and built the invitation as a mobile-first website. Guests tap a book to open it, then see the invitation, a save-the-date countdown, a swipeable carousel of wedding functions, the schedule, and the venue with directions. A deep purple and gold palette with floral and temple motifs gives it a traditional Indian wedding look.
outcome: A live invitation website that can be shared as a single link and opened on any phone. It is a personal project, so the couple's names and family details are sample content, and it has no usage numbers to share.
